Formula 1
In 2004, Bahrain became the first country in the region to host Formula 1. About BIC
Located in the heart of the Sakhir desert, Bahrain International Circuit is a unique and contemporary sports and entertainment venue that is synonymous with the highest levels of global motorsport. Featuring five different track layouts, the circuit first saw life in 2004 when the first ever Formula 1 Grand Prix took place in the country, making it the first-ever track in the Middle East to host the Formula 1 World Championship.

What's Included with F1® Experiences?
Official F1® Race Tickets
Secure the best views of Formula 1® and witness the exciting on-track action with multi-day access to any F1® circuit on the F1® calendar.
Premium Hospitality
Get premium hospitality in an exclusive F1® Experiences venue or F1 Paddock Club™ with world-class cuisine, free-flowing beverages, F1® appearances & more!
Exclusive Event Access
Join us at an exclusive event during the Grand Prix™ weekend where you can indulge in delicious lite bites & premium beverages and hear from some top F1® insiders.
Insider Extras
See the track from the drivers' perspective, walk down the famed Pit Lane, pose with the FIA Formula One World Championship™ trophy, head inside the F1® Paddock and more!
Formula 1® in Selangor
Known for its unique layout featuring a blistering back straight anchored by a famously tight hairpin, Sepang International Circuit is a favoured venue for race fans and motorsport enthusiasts alike! Conveniently located next to Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Sepang also offers easy access to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia's dynamic capital which showcases modern skyscrapers, diverse cultural influences, and vibrant street life.
The 2026 F1® season marks a special instance of the Grand Prix™ of Bahrain being held at Sepang International Circuit, so expect tickets to be highly sought-after.

How to Buy Tickets – 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
August 13, 2026
/
2026 Malaysian Grand Prix Travel Guide
/
73 Comments
/ By
Andrew Balfour
The lowdown on the best grandstands and viewing areas at Sepang International Circuit, which will host the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix on October 2-4.

The ‘2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’ is scheduled from October 2-4
Learn more about Malaysia’s surprise return to the 2026 F1 calendar
here
This post contains affiliate links. We may receive a commission if you make a purchase after clicking on one of these links.
Sepang International Circuit makes a surprise return to the F1 calendar in 2026 as host of the ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.’ Tickets are expected to go on sale in early August, only two months before race weekend. A lot has changed since Sepang last hosted Formula 1, but the circuit remains largely the same. It still offers excellent viewing opportunities from most grandstands and general admission areas, where you can generally see the cars at multiple vantage points. All grandstands are covered and there’s also an undercover section at the top of the hill stand (general admission) areas.
Tickets are
now on sale
(August 13). Prices have set by the Bahrain promoter, and are similar to the prices for the race in Bahrain. Slightly discounted tickets are available for local residents. Currently available via our supplier are tickets for the Main Grandstand, K1 Grandstand, F Grandstands and C Hillstand. F1 Experiences packages are not yet on sale.
Some of the best seats at Sepang can be found in the Main Grandstand, which spans both the back and main straights, and can hold up to 30,000 fans. When Sepang was last on the calendar in 2017, demand for tickets was not high, so most seats in the Main Grandstand offered open, unreserved seating, giving you the chance to check out different sections and views. Given that demand for this year’s race is likely to be high (despite the short 2-month lead time for sales), we expect tickets to be sold in 2026 for individual sections in the Main Grandstand. For example, seats across from the start-finish line and pit boxes of the leading teams will be more expensive than the seats at the hairpin.
You also can’t go wrong with K1 on the first corner. Grandstand F has good views, but it’s just too isolated from the atmosphere and action away from the track. If you are on a real budget, then the covered C2 Hillstand is excellent value and offers good panoramic views, but is more isolated from the rest of the action than the K2 Hillstand.
Paddock Club
: Our supplier is now on sale with tickets for the Paddock Club at the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The Paddock Club suite is located directly above the team garages at Sepang Circuit. Access includes reserved seating, gourmet meals, open bar and exciting activities such as daily pit lane walks. 3-day tickets are priced at $6,750 USD.

Grandstand F
In terms of bang for your buck, it doesn’t get much better than Grandstand F.  Situated on the Eastern central section of the track, the cheapest grandstand in Sepang offers views of more than 50% of the lap, including Turns 5 through to 8, the final hairpin bend and the main straight. The downside of the F Grandstand is that it is isolated. It’s a long way from the entrance and the main F1 Fan Zone, where the best atmosphere is found (plus more food & drink options, merch, interactive exhibits etc) .
Grandstand F Video
Grandstand K1
Situated at the end of the main straight and with a view of Turns 1 and 2, the affordable K1 grandstand is also a smart choice for fans wanting to see plenty of on-track action at Sepang. The best seats are high up in Block 1 with a front-on view of the main straight, pits and pit exit as well as the opening corners. Another reason why K1 is a good choice is its location, close to the main entrance circuit and the mall area, which should be where the main F1 Fan Zone is located.
Grandstand K1 Video
Main Grandstand
The majority of Sepang seating is located in the Main Grandstand complex, which comprises two tiers and can accommodate up to 30,000 fans. There are three main sections:
North facing grandstands, with views of the start/finish straight, pits complex and northern section of the track.
South facing grandstands, with views of most of the southern half of the track.
Tower section, situated on the final hairpin bend after the back straight and before the start-finish straight.
Both North and South sections of the Main Grandstand complex are divided into two tiers. The upper tier is smaller and offers much better viewing opportunities than the lower tier, where the views are less panoramic and partly obscured by the catch fencing – the roof is also really low in the lower section.
At the last Malaysia Grand Prix in 2017, ticket demand was quite low and the Main Grandstand was mainly sold with open, unreserved seating. But F1 is much more popular in 2026, so it seems likely that the promoter will sell individual sections of the Main grandstand at different price points. The descriptions below relate to the ‘precious stone’ naming convention last used for F1 at Sepang. When ticket details are announced for this year’s race, we will update to the new naming convention (if required). .
Main Grandstand: Sapphire (Upper) & Turquoise (Lower)
These grandstands are sitauted at the western end of the Main Grandstand and provide a great view of the first corner, where there is always lots of overtaking. Also good for some pit action (being opposite pit boxes 19-30) and the pit exit.
Main Grandstand Sapphire Video
Main Grandstand: Emerald (Upper) & Jade (Lower)
Emerald (upper tier) and Jade (lower tier) are located on the pit straight ahead after the start-finish line and with a view of pit boxes 7-18, which are normally used by the midfield teams. Good for pit action, the race start/finish and podium celebrations, but with little in the way of on-track action otherwise.
Main Grandstand Jade Video
Main Grandstand: Diamond (Upper) & Crystal (Lower)
The Diamond and Crystal grandstands are located opposite the start-finish line and pit boxes 1 to 7, where the top teams are located. A great spot to watch the pre-race preparation, start, finish and podium ceremony. Seats here are likely to be among the most expensive at the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. If on-track action is more important to you, then save yourself some money and go for grandstands such as K1 or F.
Main Grandstand Diamond Video
Main Grandstand: Ruby (Upper Tier) & Garnet (Lower Tier)
Ruby and Garnet are the upper and lower tier grandstands respectively in the north part of the Main Grandstand. Located at the eastern end of the pit straight, these grandstands don’t offer a view of the pits, but you can see Turn 5, as well as the pit entrance. The last few cars also line up on the grid for the race in front of these grandstands.
Main Grandstand Ruby Video
Main Grandstand: Tower
There are four different seating sections in the distinctive Tower section of the Main Grandstand, which is located on the final hairpin at Sepang, where it breaks up the long back and start-finish straights. The Tower lets you check out panoramic views of different parts of the circuit and is a great place to watch the action.
Tower Grandstand Video
Main Grandstand: Topaz (Upper) & Citrine (Lower)
There’s only two grandstands on the southern half of the main grandstand, Topaz on the upper tier and Citrine on the lower tier. Both offer panoramic views of the southern half of the Sepang Circuit, from Turn 8 all the way to the final Turn 13 hairpin.. The Citrine zone, on the Lower Tier of the Southern Grandstand, doesn’t offer such good panoramic views of the Southern half of the circuit.
Main Grandstand Citrine Video
Hillstand (General Admission) Tickets
Hillstand tickets are the cheapest at Sepang; there are six large, open, raised areas around the track (one of which – C2 – is partly covered) that provide a great viewing experience for budget conscious fans. Most Hillstand tickets are sold to local fans, but two sections are available for general purchase, K2 and C2. In our opinion, the best hillstand section is C2, which offers views over much of the southern half of the circuit, especially Turns 9 to 11. There also excellent panoramic views of the final turn and tower complex. It also offers protection from the rain and sun, which is very important consideration in the tropical heat of Malaysia. Nevertheless, it’s a good idea to bring along a hat, sunscreen, rain jacket, umbrella, plus a folding chair or something to sit on. The C2 area is pretty big and it wasn’t previously a problem to find a good spot here to watch the action. This may change in 2026, as we are expecting the race to be very well attended. We also recommend making the effort to visit C2 on Friday to take in the elevated views of the circuit – if ‘Free Friday’ applies at the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

About
When was the Sepang International Circuit built?
The idea for the Sepang International Circuit was born during Malaysia’s rapid development in the 1990s, when then-Prime Minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad looked to create a world-class motorsport venue as part of the country’s drive towards industrialisation. Construction began in 1997, with renowned circuit designer Hermann Tilke tasked with creating the track. The 5.543km circuit officially opened in 1999 and quickly became one of Formula 1’s most recognisable modern venues, setting the template for many of the purpose-built tracks that followed.
When was its first Grand Prix?
The inaugural Malaysian Grand Prix took place in 1999, marking F1’s first visit to Sepang. The event was memorable not only because it introduced a spectacular new circuit to the calendar, but also because it saw Michael Schumacher return from injury to help Ferrari team mate Eddie Irvine in his championship bid. Ferrari dominated the weekend, with Irvine ultimately victorious as Sepang immediately established itself as both a fan and driver favourite.
What’s the circuit like?
Sepang is among the most complete tests in Formula 1. The wide layout combines long straights, heavy-braking zones and a variety of fast, flowing corners, allowing drivers to attack from multiple racing lines. The venue is renowned for its heat and humidity, and sudden tropical downpours can transform conditions in an instant. Standout sections include the long sweep through Turns 5 and 6, and the unique final hairpin of Turn 15 that leads onto the main straight.
Why go?
Sepang has a reputation for delivering unpredictable and exciting races. The combination of challenging weather, excellent overtaking opportunities and a circuit layout that rewards driver commitment has produced countless memorable moments over the years. Away from the track, visitors can enjoy Malaysia’s vibrant culture, world-class cuisine and easy access to Kuala Lumpur, while the circuit’s proximity to Kuala Lumpur International Airport makes it one of the most convenient destinations on the F1 calendar.
Where is the best place to watch?
If you want the best all-round view, the Main Grandstand is tough to beat. Its distinctive palm-inspired canopy provides welcome shade while offering excellent views of the pit straight, the final corner and the opening sequence of turns. Alternatively, grandstands around the final hairpin are perfect for watching late-braking overtaking moves before the cars blast down the main straight. Thanks to Sepang’s wide track and open sightlines, spectators can enjoy action across multiple sections of the circuit from many vantage points.

World Motor Sport Council
The World Motor Sport Council (WMSC) has responsibility for all aspects of international motor sport. It meets at least three times a year to decide on rules, regulations, safety and development of motor sport at every level from karting to Formula One.
The WMSC is made up of the FIA President, FIA Deputy President for Sport, 7 Vice-Presidents, 14 titular members and 5 members by right. All, with the exception of the FIA President and members by right, must represent a National Sporting Authority (ASN) with at least one event entered on the International Sporting Calendar, and be of different nationalities.
The members by right are the Chairperson of the FIA Women in Motorsport Commission, the President of the FIA International Karting Commission, the Representative of the Commercial Rights Holder of the FIA Formula One World Championship, the President of the FIA Manufacturers' Committee and the President of the FIA Drivers’ Committee.
The WMSC, in its administration of international motor sport, prioritises improvements in safety and environmental standards across all forms of the sport, adopts common regulations across the various series, and nurtures motor sport’s roots by developing all forms of the sport, especially among the youth and in developing countries.

Exclusive Benefits of the F1 Paddock Club
Premium Viewing
Enjoy unrivalled views of the key action on race weekend from your prime trackside location. At the majority of circuits, the Paddock Club is situated above the team garages, overlooking the starting grid.
Fine Dining
Take your seat for a three-course gastronomic experience prepared with the finest locally-sourced ingredients and paired with fine wines. All-day refreshments and pop-up dining experiences are also available.
Exclusive Experiences

This can include guided tours of the team garage, appearances by current race drivers and team personnel, access to live telemetry and radio communications during sessions, and exclusive team merchandise gifts. More often than not, the team’s Paddock Club suite will also be directly above the pit boxes of the team!

About This Experience
Exclusive Access with F1 Paddock Club HospitalityOne of the defining features of F1 Paddock Club Hospitality is the level of exclusive access it delivers beyond traditional Formula 1 hospitality packages. Unlike general admission or standard VIP tickets, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality places guests inside the inner circle of Formula 1, offering privileged insight into the sport at the highest level.A standout inclusion is the Aramco F1 Pit Lane Walk, where guests can step into one of the most restricted areas of a Grand Prix weekend. This experience allows you to get within metres of the Formula 1 cars, observe pit crews in action, and witness the precision and preparation that goes into every race. It is a rare opportunity to see the teams, engineers and drivers up close, making it one of the most sought-after elements of any F1 Paddock Club Hospitality package.F1 Paddock Club Hospitality also provides access to exclusive appearances and live Q&A sessions with Formula 1 drivers, senior team personnel and legends of the sport. These sessions offer genuine behind-the-scenes insight into race strategy, car performance and the demands of competing in Formula 1, delivering a level of access that is not available through any other Formula 1 hospitality experience.At selected Grand Prix events, guests may also enjoy guided track tours, offering a unique perspective of the circuit from an expert-led viewpoint. In some cases, additional premium access opportunities may be available, further enhancing the overall F1 Paddock Club Hospitality experience.This combination of behind-the-scenes access, insider knowledge and proximity to the action is what sets F1 Paddock Club Hospitality apart, making it the ultimate choice for those looking to experience Formula 1 beyond the grandstands.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is F1 Paddock Club Hospitality?
F1 Paddock Club Hospitality is the most premium and exclusive hospitality experience available in Formula 1. Positioned directly above the team garages, it offers unrivalled views of the pit lane, start-finish straight and podium, placing guests at the very centre of the race weekend.Unlike standard tickets or lower-tier hospitality, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality combines trackside access with a fully inclusive luxury environment. Guests benefit from gourmet dining, premium open bars, private lounge areas and live race coverage, all delivered to a five-star standard. In addition, the experience includes exclusive behind-the-scenes access such as pit lane walks and insider appearances, making it the most immersive way to experience Formula 1.
How much does F1 Paddock Club Hospitality cost?
F1 Paddock Club Hospitality pricing varies depending on the Grand Prix, demand and level of access included within the package. As a guide, prices typically start from several thousand pounds per person for a full weekend, with the most in-demand races commanding significantly higher prices.Events such as Monaco, Silverstone, Las Vegas and Abu Dhabi are among the most sought-after, meaning F1 Paddock Club Hospitality packages at these races are often priced at a premium and sell out well in advance. Pricing can also vary based on suite location, package enhancements and additional access options. Due to limited availability at every race, securing F1 Paddock Club Hospitality early is strongly recommended.
Does F1 Paddock Club Hospitality include pit lane access?
Yes, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality includes access to the Aramco F1 Pit Lane Walk, one of the most exclusive elements of the experience. This allows guests to enter the pit lane at scheduled times during the race weekend, providing a rare opportunity to get close to the cars, garages and pit crews.During the pit lane walk, guests can observe teams preparing for the race, watch practice pit stops and gain a deeper understanding of the technical and operational side of Formula 1. This level of access is strictly controlled and not available with general admission tickets, making it a standout feature of any F1 Paddock Club Hospitality package.
Can you meet Formula 1 drivers in the Paddock Club?
F1 Paddock Club Hospitality regularly includes appearances from current Formula 1 drivers, team principals, engineers and legends of the sport. These typically take place as live Q&A sessions, interviews or stage appearances within the Paddock Club suite.While direct one-to-one meet and greets are not guaranteed, guests often have the opportunity to see drivers up close and gain insight into their experiences within Formula 1. These sessions add significant value to the overall F1 Paddock Club Hospitality experience, providing access to personalities and perspectives that are not available elsewhere at a Grand Prix.
Is F1 Paddock Club Hospitality available at every race?
Yes, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality is available at every Formula 1 Grand Prix across the global calendar. Each event delivers the same core experience, with suites located above the team garages, all-inclusive hospitality and exclusive access features included.While every destination offers its own unique atmosphere, from street circuits to historic tracks, the standard of F1 Paddock Club Hospitality remains consistent worldwide. This allows guests to attend multiple races throughout the season while enjoying a familiar, premium experience at every location.
Is F1 Paddock Club worth it?
For those seeking the highest level of access and luxury in Formula 1, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality is widely considered worth the investment. The experience goes far beyond watching the race, offering a combination of prime trackside positioning, five-star hospitality and exclusive behind-the-scenes access.Guests are not only able to view the race from the best location on the circuit, but also gain insight into the teams, drivers and operations that define Formula 1. For corporate clients, it provides a powerful platform for entertaining and relationship building, while for individuals it delivers a once-in-a-lifetime experience that cannot be replicated through standard tickets.

All tickets are dispatched a minimum of 24 hours before the eve

The Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix takes on an exciting new chapter as, in 2026, it will take place at the iconic Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia.
The Bahrain Grand Prix originally made its Formula 1 debut in 2004 as the first Grand Prix to be held in the Middle East, and since then it has become renowned for spectacular racing, dramatic overtakes and unforgettable moments.
Now, for this unique edition, the event moves to one of Formula 1's most beloved venues, offering fans a fresh way to experience a classic race weekend.
Located just outside Kuala Lumpur, the Sepang International Circuit is one of the world's most celebrated motorsport venues. Designed by renowned circuit architect Hermann Tilke, the 5.5 km layout combines 15 challenging corners, long high-speed straights and several heavy braking zones that create endless overtaking opportunities. Combined with Malaysia's tropical climate and passionate motorsport fans, the circuit consistently delivers thrilling, unpredictable racing from lights out to the chequered flag.

Why You Should Attend
The fan-favourite Sepang International Circuit is back for a one-off appearance to stand in as host of the previously called-off 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix. The single race deal presents a rare opportunity to see current day F1 racing at a circuit which holds so many memories from earlier in the 2000s. With its close proximity to the magnificent Malaysian capital, the race weekend is also a good time to see the sights in Kuala Lumpur.
Where to Watch at Sepang International Circuit
See the start of the first F1 race in Malaysia in almost a decade from the Main Grandstand, which offers the best views of the starting grid, pit stops and podium celebrations, or choose the K1 Grandstand for unrivalled views of the Sepang’s winding opening turn. General Admission has also been a popular choice in previous years when F1 has visited Malaysia, with vantage points overlooking some of the track’s action hotspots.

Malaysian Grand Prix History
Malaysia first appeared on the Formula 1 calendar in 1999 and ran annually through to the end of Sepang International Circuit’s contract in 2017. Drivers and fans loved the Kuala Lumpur track during its first stint on the calendar, thanks to its unpredictable racing and unpredictable weather. Highlights from the first iteration of the Malaysian Grand Prix included Kimi Raikkonen’s maiden F1 win in 2003, a storm-drenched half-points race won by Jenson Button in 2009 and Sebastian Vettel’s infamously controversial “Multi 21” win in 2013, where he defied team orders to pass teammate Mark Webber and take the victory.
About Sepang International Circuit
Built over the course of 14 months and opening just months before its debut on the F1 calendar in 1999, Sepang International Circuit is often considered Hermann Tilke’s best work. The track’s mix of long straights and hairpin bends, combined with its sweeping corners and humid conditions has proven the perfect recipe for memorable races. The track has hosted a range of world class motorsports over its history, from single seaters to motorcycles and endurance racing.

Guests benefit from gourmet dining, premium open bars, private lounge areas and live race coverage, all delivered to a five-star standard. In addition, the experience includes exclusive behind-the-scenes access such as pit lane walks and insider appearances, making it the most immersive way to experience Formula 1.
How much does F1 Paddock Club Hospitality cost?
F1 Paddock Club Hospitality pricing varies depending on the Grand Prix, demand and level of access included within the package. As a guide, prices typically start from several thousand pounds per person for a full weekend, with the most in-demand races commanding significantly higher prices.Events such as Monaco, Silverstone, Las Vegas and Abu Dhabi are among the most sought-after, meaning F1 Paddock Club Hospitality packages at these races are often priced at a premium and sell out well in advance. Pricing can also vary based on suite location, package enhancements and additional access options. Due to limited availability at every race, securing F1 Paddock Club Hospitality early is strongly recommended.
Does F1 Paddock Club Hospitality include pit lane access?
Yes, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality includes access to the Aramco F1 Pit Lane Walk, one of the most exclusive elements of the experience. This allows guests to enter the pit lane at scheduled times during the race weekend, providing a rare opportunity to get close to the cars, garages and pit crews.During the pit lane walk, guests can observe teams preparing for the race, watch practice pit stops and gain a deeper understanding of the technical and operational side of Formula 1. This level of access is strictly controlled and not available with general admission tickets, making it a standout feature of any F1 Paddock Club Hospitality package.
Can you meet Formula 1 drivers in the Paddock Club?
F1 Paddock Club Hospitality regularly includes appearances from current Formula 1 drivers, team principals, engineers and legends of the sport. These typically take place as live Q&A sessions, interviews or stage appearances within the Paddock Club suite.While direct one-to-one meet and greets are not guaranteed, guests often have the opportunity to see drivers up close and gain insight into their experiences within Formula 1. These sessions add significant value to the overall F1 Paddock Club Hospitality experience, providing access to personalities and perspectives that are not available elsewhere at a Grand Prix.
Is F1 Paddock Club Hospitality available at every race?
Yes, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality is available at every Formula 1 Grand Prix across the global calendar. Each event delivers the same core experience, with suites located above the team garages, all-inclusive hospitality and exclusive access features included.While every destination offers its own unique atmosphere, from street circuits to historic tracks, the standard of F1 Paddock Club Hospitality remains consistent worldwide. This allows guests to attend multiple races throughout the season while enjoying a familiar, premium experience at every location.
Is F1 Paddock Club worth it?
For those seeking the highest level of access and luxury in Formula 1, F1 Paddock Club Hospitality is widely considered worth the investment. The experience goes far beyond watching the race, offering a combination of prime trackside positioning, five-star hospitality and exclusive behind-the-scenes access.Guests are not only able to view the race from the best location on the circuit, but also gain insight into the teams, drivers and operations that define Formula 1. For corporate clients, it provides a powerful platform for entertaining and relationship building, while for individuals it delivers a once-in-a-lifetime experience that cannot be replicated through standard tickets.
When will my tickets be delivered?
All tickets are dispatched a minimum of 24 hours before the eve
